data-centers.how: Read the harvested permit documents for OKC2, CBRE, PRY, Core Scientific and Citadel, summed the engine tables by hand, searched the department permit lists for ATMOSS and Saint Francis, and searched trade press for each GEM data center plant.
data-centers.found: One add with a sum, OKC2 at 161.82 megawatts. One add with capacity blank, the Myall site in Pryor. Core Scientific is larger than GEM shows and Citadel has ten extra small engines. No generators were found at CBRE Mustang. ATMOSS and Saint Francis have no public engine documents.

local-planning-records.how: Searched the Enid planning pages and news for Project Thunderbird, the Chickasha park announcements, the Mustang and Canadian County records for the CBRE site, Pryor and Mayes County records for Google's campus, and Tulsa records for Atmoss.
local-planning-records.found: Read in full: the City of Mustang's 203 city council and planning commission agenda packets from January 2025 to November 2026, from the city's new records site, which name no power plant, generator fleet or data center. Also Stillwater's City Council, Economic Development Authority and Planning Commission papers from October 22 to November 3, 2026, which are the only ones the city's clerk system had published for that window. None names a data center, generator or gas plant. Reached but not read to the item level: Enid (the Project Thunderbird page and agenda addresses on enid.org return not found, the old agenda system returns an empty shell, and the Wayback Machine has no snapshot), Oklahoma City (agenda addresses on okc.gov return not found), Muskogee (agenda address returns not found), Pryor and Atoka (the usual city addresses gave no response, but the agenda centers on pryorcreek.org and atokaok.org were found and opened), Mayes County (a treasurer page only). News coverage says Enid held a special planning meeting on October 27, 2026 on three rezoning requests for Project Thunderbird and that Oklahoma City's council voted 6 to 3 to rezone land for a data center. Neither packet could be opened. A request to each clerk for the meeting packets is a decision for Baird. A state radio report of October 6, 2026 quotes Scale Datacenter describing a 100 megawatt plant in Oklahoma City and a second facility in southeast Oklahoma, but no document or location for that facility was found. Opened and read on November 5, 2026: the City of Atoka agenda center for March through November 2, 2026 (no data center, Artemis, generator or rezoning item, one unnamed land sale in the Heavy Industrial Park on the June 25, 2026 authority agenda), about fifty City of Pryor Creek agendas and minutes for 2026 (no Google, Myall or data center item in the searchable ones), and the five City of Tulsa council agendas for November 4, 2026 (no data center item).

odeq-onbase.how: Searched the document system by permit number, facility, company and county, and downloaded the Peoples Electric, River Valley and Hugo files.
odeq-onbase.found: The system holds only public-participation documents from 2016 on. Operating permits for the Western Farmers sites, Grand River Dam Authority sites and old 2001 plants are not in it, so the issued list is their only record.

odeq-notice-store.how: Read the stored notice evaluations for Oklahoma Cogeneration, Cushing, University of Oklahoma, Peoples Electric Marietta and Buzzard and the OG&E and PSO renewals.
odeq-notice-store.found: Read memos for Cushing, the University of Oklahoma, Oklahoma Cogeneration, the Western Farmers Anadarko turbines and two small Peoples sites. Cushing and the University are under 50 MW.

odeq-permit-lists.how: Read the four oklahoma.gov permit lists saved on 2026-11-05.
odeq-permit-lists.found: Antlers South MW, Chimney Hill MW, Cleveland SW and Canadian SW are Western Farmers operating permits. Beaver Mountain, Watts and Woka are Grand River Dam Authority sites. Arnett is a MarkWest compressor station. The Anadarko generators are four City of Anadarko emergency generators. Solarity is a solar firm. None of the lists gives a generator size above a few megawatts.

odeq-comment-pdfs.how: Read the saved public comment PDFs listed in the permit harvest.
odeq-comment-pdfs.found: They repeat the permits already read. No power plant or data center beyond those named appeared.

odeq-air-pages.how: Opened the air permit list page. The old deq.ok.gov notice pages now redirect to oklahoma.gov/deq.html.
odeq-air-pages.found: The old deq.ok.gov air quality address redirects to the agency home page, the public review page on oklahoma.gov returns not found, and the Wayback Machine has no saved copy of the permit pages I tried.

spp-eras.how: Read the ERAS rows in the active queue list and the SPP resource adequacy and generator interconnection pages.
spp-eras.found: Seven ERAS rows in Oklahoma, all with fully executed agreements. Sponsors are not published. Five match GEM units in place and year, with size gaps staged as question cards. Redbud 186 MW is a question.

occ-pud-dockets.found: PUD2025-000084 is a battery. PUD2026-000031 is Google service agreements and solar purchase agreements. PUD2026-000046 is a tariff. PUD2025-000064 approves Northeastern units 5 and 6, which GEM already has. No new gas unit.

occ-ecf.how: Searched the commission's filing system by cause number for the same four causes and read the entries returned.
occ-ecf.found: The filings listed matched the WebLink copies, with no gas unit not already in GEM.

occ-weblink.how: Used the anonymous WebLink search service to list and download documents, and exported and read the scanned order for the Public Service Company of Oklahoma preapproval.
occ-weblink.found: Applications and testimony for the four causes were read. Scanned orders needed text recognition.

occ-pud-reports.how: Read the OG&E 2025 resource plan copy and the March 2026 nuclear feasibility study in the commission reports folder.
occ-pud-reports.found: Nothing new for gas units beyond what GEM and the utility plans already carry.

oge-irp.how: Read the OG&E 2026 plan PDF, the state commission copy of the 2025 plan, and the OG&E annual report to the SEC.
oge-irp.found: GEM already holds Horseshoe Lake units 11 to 15 and the Tinker project. No unsited committed gas unit is missing. The next full plan is the 2027 triennial plan.

pso-irp.how: Read the 2024 plan and the 2026 refresh report resource tables and text.
pso-irp.found: Northeastern 5 and 6 start year is 2029, and the plan lists planning retirement years for six gas plants. The new 4,000 MW request for proposals names no site.

sec-edgar.found: The report names Tinker Air Force Base and Horseshoe Lake units 11 to 14 as committed projects, all already in GEM.

wfec.how: Read the cooperative home page, tried its generation and news pages, and read trade press on the Hugo and Anadarko work.
wfec.found: Hugo Site A and Site B and Anadarko Roulet 12 and 13 are already in GEM with matching size and dates. The cooperative home page names no further gas unit.

aeci.how: Read the Bristow Energy Center page and a trade press article on the turbine order.
aeci.found: Bristow is a 420 MW net natural gas peaking plant owned by Associated Electric Cooperative, online in late 2029, which matches GEM.

grda.how: Read the authority home page, trade press on Unit 4, and the Southwest Power Pool row for ASGI-2015-004.
grda.found: Unit 4 is a 426 MW simple cycle turbine dedicated in September 2026, matching GEM. The Nowata request ASGI-2015-004 matches the Coffeyville, Kansas city engine plant, which is in Kansas.

ompa.how: Read the authority news pages, the state air permit application, completeness letter and notice of filing.
ompa.found: A second Lamb turbine, 90 MW, is in a Tier II construction permit review. It is added as a new unit.

evergy-irp.found: The deck shows Evergy fleet additions and retirements as totals and names no Spring Creek change. Spring Creek stays as in GEM.

tenaska-kiamichi.how: Read the Tenaska Kiamichi fact sheet from May 2026.
tenaska-kiamichi.found: The sheet gives owner Kiowa Power Partners, 1,220 MW, and operation since April 2003, matching GEM. It names no uprate or ownership change.

eia-860m.how: Read the Operating, Planned, Retired and Canceled sheets of the September 2026 monthly file for Oklahoma, and compared each gas and oil plant with GEM unit by unit.
eia-860m.found: Two plants GEM lacks at the threshold: Georgia-Pacific Muskogee and Centrahoma. Seven plants below 50 MW. Every planned unit matches GEM. Retirements since 2020 at 50 MW or more are already in GEM. Disagreements on Grand River, Ripley, Mustang, Horseshoe Lake, Northeastern and Mooreland are in question cards.

eia-860.how: Downloaded the 2025 annual survey and read the generator, plant and owner tables for Oklahoma.
eia-860.found: Addresses and points for the added plants, and owner shares that agree with GEM except at Kiamichi, which has a question card.

eip-oil-gas-watch.found: The EIP status disagreements on Anadarko, Grand River, Horseshoe Lake and Northeastern are each settled with a question card that cites the federal file and an utility or press source. Chickasha stays cancelled.

possible-updates-sheet.how: Read the gas and oil tab through the work profile in read-only mode and saved a copy under the scope work folder. Filtered by country and by plant names.
possible-updates-sheet.found: Every Oklahoma row is marked done: the Mitsubishi coal-to-gas row, Green Country, the Chickasha data center, Northeastern, the Core Scientific Muskogee site, the two OG&E plan rows and the Grand River unit 4 row. Each is already matched by a GEM plant or by an existing record in this scope.

captive-lng-sheet.how: Read the captive LNG match file for Oklahoma.
captive-lng-sheet.found: The file has no Oklahoma terminals. The only data center match is the Chickasha site. A search of Oklahoma LNG facilities found no on-site generation at 50 MW.

state-news.how: Searched Oklahoma trade and local press since 2024 for the gas plants of each utility and chased each lead to a primary document.
state-news.found: The Tinker turbines, the Horseshoe Lake approval, the Grand River unit 4 dedication and the Northeastern conversion plan were confirmed. No unlisted gas plant was found beyond the added ones.

10362.evidence: The monthly federal generator file for September 2026 lists three operating natural gas steam turbines at Georgia-Pacific Muskogee, plant 10362: GEN1 25 MW from 1979, GEN2 44.5 MW from 1980 and GEN3 44.5 MW from 1982, 114 MW in total. A 2016 notice from the state environmental agency describes the mill's boilers feeding electric steam turbines. Added as a new plant, with a question card on GEM's Fort James plant.

63628.evidence: Plant 63628 Tinker sits on the point of GEM's Tinker Air Force Base power station. The unit capacities differ, so a question card covers it.

6000-n-shartel-ave-llc-oklahoma-city.note: Nineteen natural gas engines, 161.82 megawatts, from the September 2026 application. Added as a new plant with two units. None of the first 11 engines is operating, because start-up is planned for the first quarter of 2027.

tenmark-mustang-industri-cbre-okc-site.note: The draft Title V permit renewal lists boilers, two fire pump engines of 215 and 340 horsepower and three emergency generator engines with no rating, at the former Xerox site in Canadian County. No data center is named in the permit, so no sum can be made, and nothing suggests the three generators reach 50 megawatts. Trade press says Tenmark Holdings bought the Xerox properties in a sale and leaseback with Xerox still leasing, and no report links the site to a data center. No Mustang, Canadian County or Oklahoma City agenda naming a data center there turned up in web searches.

pry-data-storage-facilit-pry-data-storag.note: The permit evaluation of November 5, 2025 keeps the engine list confidential, so no sum can be made by hand. Added with capacity blank. Myall LLC bought the land for Google's Pryor campus, so this is very likely Google's Pryor campus at the MidAmerica Industrial Park, though the permit does not name Google.

atmoss-data-center.note: The department list of permits issued in the past year shows permit 2026-0025-O for Atmoss LLC, ATMOSS Data Center, Wagoner County, issued January 15, 2026. The O class is a minor source permit, and the department's document store holds no documents for it. Atmoss LLC is the developer of Meta's Project Anthem campus in east Tulsa according to a data center directory, and no on-site gas plant is reported for it. No engine list exists in any public place found, so no sum can be made. A request for the permit file from the department's records office is a decision for Baird.

saint-francis-hospital-data-center.note: The department list shows permit 2026-0469-O for Saint Francis Health System, Saint Francis Hospital Data Center, Tulsa, issued June 29, 2026. It is a minor source permit with no public documents in the document store. A hospital data center backup fleet is very unlikely to reach 50 megawatts. No engine list was found, so no sum is possible. The earlier Saint Francis evaluation in the notice store, permit 2016-1075-TVR, covers the hospital campus and not a data center fleet. Local records: the Tulsa City Council agendas for November 4, 2026 were opened, covering the regular meeting, the pre-regular meeting and the budget, public works and urban and economic development committee meetings. None names a Saint Francis data center, a generator fleet or a hospital item. News coverage of the Tulsa city council data center moratorium names no Saint Francis project either. Tulsa County zoning records were not opened.

artemis-data-center-artemis-data-center.note: The department facility table lists Artemis Data Center, Atoka, with a water permit only and no air permit or generator documents. No gas or backup fleet is reported for it in the news results searched. Local records: the City of Atoka agenda center was opened for every city council and planning agenda and set of minutes from March through November 2, 2026. None names Artemis, a data center, a generator fleet or a rezoning. The Atoka Industrial Development Authority agenda of June 25, 2026 lists a land sale in the Heavy Industrial Park with the buyer not named. Atoka County records were not opened.

one-nuclear-energy-one-nuclear-power-sta.note: GEM lists ONE Nuclear power station 1 as announced at 1,000 megawatts. No air permit or newer public record was found that changes it.

lightfield-energy-chickasha.note: GEM lists the Chickasha industrial park power station as cancelled at 500 megawatts. The 2025 reports describe a plan by developer Chet Hitt and Lightfield Energy with no permit, and no 2026 report was found that revives it, so cancelled still fits.

plainsmen-holdings-llc-1-enid.note: GEM lists Project Thunderbird Data Center power station as pre-construction at 3,300 megawatts. The City of Enid says only a rezoning request is under review and nothing is approved, so announced may fit better than pre-construction.

core-scientific-inc-100-port-muskogee.note: The July 2026 application sums to 314.0 megawatts against GEM's 283.1. A question card covers it.

citadel-asset-ventures-l-sperry.note: The 108 large engines match GEM. Ten smaller backup engines are not in GEM. A question card covers them.

scale-southeast-oklahoma-facility.note: A state radio report of October 6, 2026 says Scale Datacenter is also building a facility in southeast Oklahoma. No permit, county record or news item naming its site or its power was found, and the department permit lists show no Scale application besides OKC2.

other-operators-stack-skybox-prime-meta-.note: Searches for Stack, Skybox, Prime Data, Meta and Microsoft in Oklahoma found no air permit or report of an on-site gas or backup engine fleet. Meta's Project Anthem campus in east Tulsa is built by Atmoss LLC and no on-site plant is reported. A state radio report of August 6, 2026 says most Oklahoma data centers, including Luther Horizon, Project Mustang in Claremore and IREN's Kiowa campus, plan to buy grid power from local utilities. Local records: the Tulsa City Council agendas for November 4, 2026 were opened and name none of Stack, Skybox, Prime Data, Meta or Microsoft, and no generator fleet. The Oklahoma City council agenda addresses on okc.gov returned not found, so Oklahoma City council and planning records were not read.

google-stillwater-and-pryor-expansion.note: Google and OG&E announced a grid supply deal in spring 2026 for the Muskogee and Stillwater data centers. An April 2026 trade report says no on-site gas project by Google has been publicly confirmed in Oklahoma. Stillwater's council papers of November 2, 2026 mention no data center. Local records: the City of Pryor Creek agenda center was opened for about fifty city council and planning agendas and minutes from January to October 2026. Many are scanned pages that could not be searched as text, and the searchable ones name no Google, Myall or data center item. The Stillwater City Council, Economic Development Authority and Planning Commission papers of October 22 to November 3, 2026 name no data center. Mayes County and Payne County planning records were not opened.

SPP GEN-2024-340.evidence: The SPP queue lists GEN-2024-340, 1440 MW of gas at the Riverside to Redbud 345 kilovolt line (AEP), commercial operation January 1, 2032. GEM has no matching plant. It is added as announced with the owner blank because SPP does not publish the company.

SPP GEN-2024-334.evidence: The SPP queue lists GEN-2024-334, 103 MW of gas at the Ranch Road 345 kilovolt substation (OG&E), commercial operation June 1, 2029. GEM has no matching plant. It is added as announced with the owner blank because SPP does not publish the company.

SPP GEN-2024-321.evidence: The SPP queue lists GEN-2024-321, 507 MW of gas at the Seminole 345 kilovolt substation (OG&E), commercial operation April 30, 2030. GEM has no matching plant. It is added as announced with the owner blank because SPP does not publish the company.

SPP GEN-2024-299.evidence: The SPP queue lists GEN-2024-299, 744 MW of gas at the AES 5 345 kilovolt substation (OG&E), commercial operation May 1, 2032. GEM has no matching plant. It is added as announced with the owner blank because SPP does not publish the company.

SPP GEN-2024-293.evidence: The SPP queue lists GEN-2024-293, 248 MW of gas at the Muskogee 345 kilovolt substation (OG&E), commercial operation May 1, 2033. GEM has no matching plant. It is added as announced with the owner blank because SPP does not publish the company.

SPP GEN-2024-128.evidence: The SPP queue lists GEN-2024-128, 726.9 MW of gas at the Gracemont to Lawton 345 kilovolt line (OG&E), commercial operation December 31, 2030. GEM has no matching plant. It is added as announced with the owner blank because SPP does not publish the company.

SPP GEN-2024-013.evidence: The SPP queue lists GEN-2024-013, 496 MW of gas at the Norman Hills 345 kilovolt substation (OG&E), commercial operation January 1, 2030. GEM has no matching plant. It is added as announced with the owner blank because SPP does not publish the company. The same 496 MW size appears at Horseshoe Lake in ERAS-2025-010, but that row is at a different substation, so the two are kept apart.

SPP GEN-2024-323.evidence: The SPP queue lists a 372 MW gas request at the ITC Hugo 7 substation in Choctaw County with commercial operation on May 1, 2029. GEM's Hugo Site B is 342 MW, pre-construction, 2029, owned by Western Farmers Electric Cooperative. They are probably the same project, so a question card is staged instead of a new plant. The question card is in the state shard.

SPP GEN-2026-SR34.evidence: A 75 MW thermal surplus request at the WFEC Hugo 138 kilovolt point in Fort Towson, commercial operation April 1, 2029. GEM's Hugo Site A is 73.5 MW, pre-construction, 2029. It is the same project. No surplus study report is posted yet, so the 1.5 MW difference cannot be explained.

SPP GEN-2024-GR1.evidence: A 492 MW combustion turbine replacement request at Horseshoe Lake 138 kilovolt, agreement fully executed, commercial operation December 31, 2026. GEM already carries Horseshoe Lake units 11 and 12 (224 MW each, 448 MW, operating 2026). The queue and GEM sizes differ by a few percent, which is a rating difference, so nothing is staged.

SPP GEN-2023-GR2.evidence: A 94.2 MW gas replacement request at Tinker Air Force Base 138 kilovolt, agreement fully executed, commercial operation May 1, 2026. GEM already carries Tinker units 1 and 2 (96 MW, operating 2026). The queue and GEM sizes differ by a few percent, which is a rating difference, so nothing is staged.

SPP GEN-2023-GR1.evidence: A 97.5 MW gas replacement request at Anadarko Power Plant 69 kilovolt, owned by Western Farmers Electric Cooperative, agreement fully executed, commercial operation December 1, 2025. GEM already carries Anadarko Roulet units 12 and 13 (50.2 MW each, construction 2026). The queue and GEM sizes differ by a few percent, which is a rating difference, so nothing is staged.

SPP ERAS-2025-026.evidence: A 775.2 MW combined cycle request at the Oklaunion to Lawton East Side 345 kilovolt line in Lawton, agreement fully executed, commercial operation November 30, 2029. GEM's Comanche (OK) units CC2 and CC3 are 686.4 MW each, pre-construction, 2029, owned by Public Service Company of Oklahoma. This row and ERAS-2025-024 are the two blocks. A question card covers the size gap.

SPP ERAS-2025-024.evidence: A 775.2 MW combined cycle request at the Comanche 138 kilovolt substation in Lawton, agreement fully executed, commercial operation November 30, 2029. It is the second block with ERAS-2025-026 and matches GEM's Comanche (OK) CC2 and CC3 in place and year. A question card covers the size gap.

SPP ERAS-2025-023.evidence: A 513 MW combustion turbine request at the Northeastern 345 kilovolt substation in Oologah, agreement fully executed, commercial operation December 15, 2029. GEM's Northeastern units 5 and 6 are 225 MW each, 450 MW, pre-construction, due 2028. A question card covers the size and year gap.

SPP ERAS-2025-010.evidence: A 496 MW combustion turbine request at Horseshoe Lake 138 kilovolt, agreement fully executed, commercial operation January 1, 2029. GEM's Horseshoe Lake units 13 and 14 are 224 MW each, 448 MW, pre-construction, due 2029. A question card covers the size gap.

SPP ERAS-2025-004.evidence: A 756.2 MW combined cycle request at Horseshoe Lake 138 kilovolt, agreement fully executed, commercial operation October 3, 2030. GEM's Horseshoe Lake unit 15 is 755 MW, pre-construction, due 2031. The size matches. A question card covers the year.

SPP ERAS-2025-003.evidence: A 186 MW combined cycle request at the Redbud 345 kilovolt substation near Luther, agreement fully executed, in service date October 24, 2025 and commercial operation January 18, 2027. GEM's Redbud plant has four units of 358 MW, all operating, and no 186 MW unit. It may be an uprate of a Redbud unit or a new add-on. A question card asks which. The question card is in the state shard.

SPP ASGI-2015-004.evidence: The SPP row lists 56.4 MW of reciprocating engines owned by the Grand River Dam Authority, in service November 2015, at the Coffeyville City 69 kilovolt point, with Nowata as the nearest town. The Coffeyville point is in Kansas, so the Nowata label looks like a queue data error. No Oklahoma plant is added.

us-ok:new:okc2-scale-datacenter-power-st.evidence: The two batch neighbors are the separate SPP surplus diesel fleets at Horseshoe Lake and Mustang, which sit at other substations. OKC2 is a data center plant with Wartsila engines and no GEM plant of any fuel carries its name.

us-ok:new:myall-pryor-data-center-power-.evidence: Chouteau power station is a gas plant 5.3 kilometers away and Grand River Energy Center is a utility plant 7.0 kilometers away. Neither is a data center and neither has the Myall emergency generator engines. The SPP SR19 diesel fleet is at the Maid substation, a different site.

us-ok:new:spp-gen-2025-sr19-maid-diesel-.evidence: Chouteau power station and Grand River Energy Center are existing plants in the same county with different fuels and owners. The SPP study describes 31 new diesel engines at the Maid substation, sharing the point of interconnection with a battery, so this is a separate new plant.

us-ok:new:spp-gen-2025-sr21-tulsa-power-.evidence: GEM has a Tulsa power station of gas units.
